> 習坎。有孚維心，亨。行有尚。

Hexagram 29 is the doubled trigram of water, and it is the seventh character in this series that commentary has taken apart as a picture.

## 坎 is 從土，欠聲

說文: 坎，陷也。從土，欠聲.

Phonetic: 土 as the semantic side, 欠 as the sound. Original sense: a pit, a hollow, something that gives way underfoot.

The count is now seven: 訟 從言公聲, 謙 從言兼聲, 觀 從見雚聲, 賁 從貝卉聲, 復 從彳复聲, 妄 從女亡聲, and 坎. Plus 剝, where the error ran the other way and a 亦聲 was dropped.

The treatment does not change with repetition: if the construction is not settled, interpretation steps in and replaces the character's sense. 坎 means a pit. It is not "earth plus a yawn, meaning both."

## 習坎, two readings

習 has two old glosses: 重, doubled — two 坎 stacked, one peril on another, which is what the 彖 says (重險也); and 便習, being accustomed to danger through long residence in it.

This book takes the first, because it agrees with the 彖.

The second reading is very smooth, and it is derived backwards from how a person behaves in danger. It is not how the name is built.

## 維心

有孚維心，亨.

維 is the cord — the same character as in 隨's 乃從維之.

So the trust is tied to the heart, held there, in a place that has no footing.

And the judgement is 亨 — unimpeded — in the middle of a doubled pit. Which is the hexagram's whole claim: the passage is not through the water, it is a condition of the heart that holds while the water is there.

## 窞: a pit inside a pit

初六 習坎，入于坎窞，凶.

窞 is the dark hole at the bottom of a pit — the pit within the pit.

凶 on the first line, unqualified, because the position is the very bottom of a doubled danger: falling into the hollow of the hollow.

## 險且枕

六三 來之坎坎，險且枕，入于坎窞，勿用.

枕: to stop, to lie low, to lean (old glosses give 止, 伏, 倚). The later reading "to pillow on the danger" turns a noun into a verb and loses the line.

So: forward is a pit, backward is a pit; the danger is in front and there is nothing to do but lie still. And then it falls in anyway. 勿用 — do not act.

Which is the only instruction in the hexagram that is purely negative, and it is placed at the exact middle of the doubled peril.

## 樽酒，簋貳，用缶

六四: a jug of wine, two baskets of grain, earthenware vessels.

The most reduced possible offering, in the plainest possible ware.

納約自牖 — 牖 is the window. The simple agreement enters through the window, not through the door.

So whatever passes between people in the middle of a danger does not go through the official opening. It goes through a gap, plainly, and that is why the line is 終無咎.

## 徽纆 and 叢棘

上六: 係用徽纆，寘于叢棘，三歲不得，凶.

徽 is three-stranded rope; 纆 is two-stranded (說文 ties it to prison affairs). 叢棘: thorn planted around a jail, the archaic image of confinement.

Three years and not obtained.

Which is the far end of 坎: danger that has become an enclosure, and an enclosure that has become a duration.

## 水洊至

洊 is again, in succession. One wave comes, and another behind it, without a break.

習坎's 習 is audible in that image: the danger is not one event, it is a series.

And the 象's instruction: 常德行，習教事 — keep the conduct constant, practise the work of teaching.

Which is a strange response to a flood and an exact one: what survives a series is not a defence, it is a habit. The water keeps coming; the thing that holds is the thing done repeatedly.

## The test

Take a difficulty you are inside. Ask whether it is one pit or two stacked, and then ask what your 維 is — the cord your trust is tied to. The hexagram does not offer a way out of the water. It offers a place to tie to while you are in it.
